newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: U.S., EU agree new drug-busting deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S., EU agree new drug-busting deal.

text.p: The United States and the European Union pledged on Wednesday to step up a joint battle against illegal drugs and signed a pact to keep the chemicals used to make synthetic drugs out of the hands of traffickers.
Speaking at the twice-yearly U.S.-EU summit, U.S. President Bill Clinton said the agreement would "strengthen our fights to keep illegal drugs out of our neighbourhoods".

In what was described as the first formal EU-U.S. anti-drug initiative, the two sides agreed to swap information on transactions in regulated chemicals to allow for easier identification of suspicious shipments.
The agreement also placed restrictions on the shipment of some types of chemicals, requiring special authorisation from importing country officals.

Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, whose country holds the EU presidency, said the two sides had also agreed to step up cooperation in fighting drugs in the Caribbean, where a number of EU countries have territories or retain influence.
"This includes joint studies on maritime cooperation, exchange of information and equipment and training of police and judicial authorities," Kok said.
